issue.title: quality: adapter/preset layer declares gates it never reconciles, applies, or reports as gaps
issue.body:
## Situation

A consumer repo — `cmanki`, a TypeScript/Svelte/Cloudflare-Workers app — has had
`.agents/quality-adapter.yaml` since early in its life and has dispatched
`charness:quality` 54 times and `charness:setup` 11 times. Its adapter declares
`preset_lineage: [typescript-quality]` and
`canonical_markdown_surfaces: [AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md]`.

## Experience

The operator asked why the repo had no linter beyond `eslint:recommended`, no
pre-commit hook, and an agent instruction file that had grown past Claude Code's
large-memory warning floor. Auditing it, the state was:

- `eslint.config.js` with no `complexity`, `max-lines-per-function`,
  `max-statements`, `max-depth`, `max-params`, or `max-len` rule
- no pre-commit hook, no pre-push hook, no CI workflow
- no dead-code, duplication, lockfile, secret-scan, or docs-link gate
- `src/App.svelte` at 1,587 code lines; `worker/index.ts` `handleRequest` at
  cyclomatic complexity 68
- `AGENTS.md` at 41,041 characters, past the ~40,000-character large-memory floor
- `gate_commands: [npm run quality:report]` — one command, in a repo with 21 npm
  scripts including `lint`, `check`, and `test`, so the standing quality gate
  never invoked the linter at all

All of this is inside `quality`'s stated scope. None of it was ever recorded as
an `unresolved enforcement gap`, which the skill's own invariant requires.

## Evidence

**Preset lineage recorded but never reconciled.**
`presets/typescript-quality.md` prescribes verbatim: "static gates: `eslint` with
a standing `complexity` rule, plus `tsc --noEmit`"; "`complexity: [\"error\", 15]`
as a practical starting hard gate"; "confidence extras when justified: coverage,
`knip`, `secretlint` or `gitleaks`"; "`tokei` for SLOC inventory". None landed.
`bootstrap_adapter.py` reports every field as `"preserved"` — it preserves the
declaration without diffing the adapter against what the named preset prescribes.

**Adapter gate-design inventory finds nothing on a defective adapter.**
`inventory_adapter_gate_design.py` returned `findings: []` while
`coverage_floor_policy` pointed at `lefthook.yml`, `.github/workflows/*.yml`, and
`scripts/coverage-floor-exemptions.txt` — none of which exist in that repo — and
while `gate_commands` omitted every repo lint and test script. Separately,
`nose_inventory_paths` was unset, so clone scanning silently covered only
`scripts` and `skills/support`; adding `src` and `worker` took ranked clone
families from 14 to 91.

**Instruction files are declared as a surface but unreachable by the rules.**
The adapter declares `canonical_markdown_surfaces: [AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md]` and
`skill_ergonomics_gate_rules: [dated_incident_in_core, long_core,
progressive_disclosure_risk, ...]`, but no path connects them.
`skill_ergonomics_skill_paths` is the only input and accepts `SKILL.md` only —
adding `AGENTS.md` is a silent no-op (`inventory_skill_ergonomics.py` prints
`checked 2 skill(s)` and drops it without warning). So `dated_incident_in_core`
and `long_core` have never been evaluated against that 41 KB file, which was
accreting dated incident narrative because the repo's own rules told agents to
record counter-arguments and corrections with no destination split.

`references/entrypoint-docs-ergonomics.md` does catch it. Run manually it reports
`AGENTS.md: heuristics=long_entrypoint, host_instruction_runbook_pressure` and
`docs/handoff.md: lines=1818 long_entrypoint`. But it is an `on_demand_reads`
reference with an advisory-by-design helper whose stated subject is "entrypoint
docs" (README/install), and `progressive_disclosure_risk` in
`validate_skill_ergonomics.py` is scoped to `{"public"}` skills.

**Dead-code advisory reports a false green on a non-Python repo.**
`run_dead_code_advisory.py` is vulture-based and globs `git ls-files -- '*.py'`.
On this TypeScript repo it printed `Primary (80%): clean (0 findings)` /
`Sweep (60%): clean (0 findings)` with no language caveat. Installing `knip`
immediately surfaced two undeclared dependencies (`@codemirror/commands`,
`@codemirror/language`, relying on hoisting), one unused dependency, 25 unused
exports, and a fully orphaned 127-line component whose feature — showing a
release note once per version — had silently regressed when the surface moved to
a page.

**`setup` mandates instruction-file content it never measures.**
`setup_agent_docs_lib.py` and `setup_commit_discipline_lib.py` require
`## Skill Routing`, `## Dynamic Workflows`, commit-discipline, and
subagent-delegation wording inside `AGENTS.md` via
`extract_section(agents_text, ...)`. In this repo that is 94 lines. After cutting
everything else to a pointer-style file, those 94 lines are 61% of what remains.

**A sibling repo in the same org shows the gap size.**
`craken-agents` runs, split across commit and push boundaries: `biome`
format+lint, `lockfile-lint`, `dependency-cruiser`, `knip`, `jscpd`,
`awiki lint` for docs, `vitest` with coverage, `stryker` mutation testing,
`gitleaks`, and husky-managed pre-commit/pre-push hooks. Its `AGENTS.md` is 20
lines pointing to a `docs/` wiki with `docs/index.md` as the entry point.

## Repro

```
# consumer repo with .agents/quality-adapter.yaml, preset_lineage: [typescript-quality]
python3 $SKILL_DIR/scripts/bootstrap_adapter.py --repo-root .            # all fields "preserved"
python3 $SKILL_DIR/scripts/inventory_adapter_gate_design.py --repo-root . # findings: []
python3 $SKILL_DIR/scripts/run_dead_code_advisory.py --repo-root .        # "clean" on a TS repo
python3 $SKILL_DIR/scripts/inventory_skill_ergonomics.py --repo-root .    # skips AGENTS.md silently
python3 $SKILL_DIR/scripts/inventory_entrypoint_docs_ergonomics.py --repo-root .  # correctly flags it
```

## Impact

An adapter can name a preset, name the surfaces it cares about, and name the
ergonomics rules to apply, and still receive no gate and no gap report for
months. The failure is quiet in both directions: the helpers return clean or
empty rather than "not applicable" or "not reachable", so repeated `quality` runs
read as healthy. The operator discovered the gap by reading a sibling repo, not
from any charness output. Meanwhile `setup` was actively growing the one file
that `quality`'s own long-core rule could not see.

## Weak direction — non-binding

Not a design decision, just where a receiving agent might look first: making
unreachable configuration loud rather than silent (unknown entries in
`skill_ergonomics_skill_paths`, dangling `coverage_floor_policy` paths, a
language-unsupported dead-code scan) would surface four of the findings above
without any new gate. The `preset_lineage` reconciliation and the
`setup`-versus-long-core tension are separate calls and may belong in their own
issues.

## Source

- Source origin: repo-audit
- Source identity: local consumer repo `/home/hwidong/codes/cmanki` at commit
  `aac5fec`, audited 2026-08-07
- access: local
- freshness: 2026-08-07
- Source preservation: re-read obligation
- Re-read obligation: re-run the five repro commands against a TypeScript
  consumer repo before resolving or closing; the numbers above are from a single
  repo at one commit and the repo has since had gates added by hand, so the
  original state is only reproducible from history.
